parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction meaning quietly
to compliment someone is to praise them

explanation.surface: Someone advises that a little quiet flattery is the way to show you value a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise something is to assess its worth, which is what valuing it means.

clue.text: Use art to raise the wind

indicators.note: to raise is to build up, so the letters of use art are constructed into a new word

explanation.surface: An instruction to use art to whip up a wind, perhaps by magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise' signals building USE ART into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical poetry the south wind is named after a Latin god.

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a bed is a formally laid-out area of flowers in a garden

explanation.surface: Someone dug the ground ready for the ornamental garden planting.
explanation.walkthrough: The gardening surface hides the sense 'investigated': dug into a matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig into something is to explore it searchingly, as an investigator does.

clue.text: Article on a jerk-the old buffoon!

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: An exclamation about an article on a fool from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: As a noun this word once meant a clown or grotesque performer, a sense now archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: In older English a grotesque performer or clown was given this name.

definitions.meaning: a relative by marriage: a husband or wife's son from an earlier union
to board a bus is to step on it, split as two words

explanation.definitionFit: A spouse's son is a family relative; one who climbs onto a vehicle gets on it.

clue.text: Wiped out, as deer might well be

indicators.note: the words as deer might well be rearranged into something else, so they are anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A remark that a herd of deer could easily be wiped out, by hunters perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might well be' signals that AS DEER can be rearranged; the letters give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erased has been rubbed out or obliterated, so it is wiped out.

clue.text: Strike a number with unpaid debts as really extortionate

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
C is the Roman numeral 100, a number
IOUs are written acknowledgements of money owed

explanation.surface: A creditor hits someone with a pile of unpaid debts as being plain extortion.
explanation.definitionFit: Greedy and grasping in the extreme describes someone whose demands are wildly extortionate.

parts.note: wee, Scots for small, can mean short
an age is a long while

explanation.surface: A small deficit that lasts only a little while.
explanation.walkthrough: A short age is a small while: the clue is a cryptic play on the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack or insufficiency is a deficit.

clue.text: Finding school filling in time, blow up

indicators.note: the school fills the inside of the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A school fills up its timetable and things blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON College is a well-known English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: To explode a bomb is to blow it up.

parts.note: pretends to mean the tree that yields fragrant sandalwood, but reads as the wooden form that sits inside footwear to keep its shape

explanation.walkthrough: Sandalwood is a fragrant timber, but split it as 'sandal wood': the wooden device placed inside a shoe or sandal to hold its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden foot-shaped form inserted into footwear is a piece of wood found in a sandal.

clue.text: A growth that may cause stupor

indicators.note: the letters of the word stupor are what a rearrangement may cause, so the two words are anagrams of each other

explanation.surface: A medical remark about some growth or tumour that may leave a patient in a stupor.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the answer, rearranged, may cause STUPOR; read the other way, 'may cause' is the anagram signal on 'stupor'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoot or bud on a plant is a new growth.

parts.note: US is short for United States, hence American
ED, the editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: An American reporter is exploited.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exploited has been made use of.

definitions.meaning: to use a power or right is to exercise it, as a verb
drill is repeated practice, as in physical training routines

explanation.definitionFit: One exercises an option by using it; drills are practice routines, the noun sense.

parts.note: CU is the chemical symbol for copper, a little abbreviation
a tin is a can, as for food

explanation.surface: A small police officer is allowed to step in and intervene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little copper' suggests a young policeman; it is the short symbol for the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To butt into a conversation or dance is to interrupt, which is to intervene.

parts.note: hard cash usually means ready money, but here it is money that is literally hard: metal pieces rather than paper

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the literal reading: money made of metal is physically hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal disc used as money is cash in a hard form.

definitions.meaning: offers or approaches made to start negotiations
pieces written in musical notes, the orchestral openings before an opera

explanation.definitionFit: Peace approaches are offers; orchestral introductions are music written in notes.

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number, so it stands for many
rough can mean hard, as in a rough time

explanation.surface: Something is giving a lot of people a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' refers to the answer to 7 Down, SHORTAGE: this answer is a shortage of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spell without rain is a shortage, specifically of water.

clue.text: Beats up a top man for being flashy

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for beats is read backwards

parts.note: raps are blows or beats
a king is the man at the top

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a boss for being showy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAPS to SPAR; 'Beats up' reads as an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving off sparks or flashes of light is a flashy display.

parts.note: re means about, concerning
part means some, a portion

indicators.note: duplicated means the musical key letter appears twice

parts.note: E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A joke about some copied key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duplicated' doubles E to make EE.
explanation.definitionFit: Witty banter consists of quick retorts or quips.

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before or beforehand
something conveyed has been sent

explanation.surface: A question about whether an offer was delivered ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a gift, the answer is something conveyed beforehand; split, it is pre + sent.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer something formally, such as a proposal, is to put it forward or hand it over.

parts.note: to can mean until, as in 'nine to five'
I is the Roman numeral 1 and L the Roman numeral 50

explanation.surface: Someone toils right through until ten to two.
explanation.walkthrough: '1.50' looks like a clock time; it is the Roman numerals for one and fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: To labour strenuously is to work hard.

definitions.meaning: a large number of people, a multitude
a person who receives and entertains guests

explanation.definitionFit: A multitude can be called a great throng; the person who receives guests at a party entertains them.

indicators.note: the pledge contains, involves, the next pieces

parts.note: to hock something is to pawn it as a pledge
DD is Doctor of Divinity, so a divine or clergyman

explanation.surface: A promise involving a holy fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A North Atlantic food fish of the cod family.

definitions.meaning: an instant, as in 'in a flash'

explanation.definitionFit: A very brief instant is a flash; matters of great import are of concern.

indicators.note: uncertain suggests the letters of as one's are unsettled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's mood is as unpredictable as their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncertain' rearranges AS ONE'S, the S counting as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To season is to moderate or soften, as justice is tempered with mercy.

clue.text: Cook is corrupt since going inside

indicators.note: the word for since is put inside the word for corrupt

parts.note: to corrupt or decay is to rot
as can mean since, as in 'as it rained, we stayed in'

explanation.surface: A complaint that a chef is dishonest because they are going to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going inside' reads as being jailed, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook meat in an oven is a common way of preparing it.

parts.note: looks like stirring up resentment, but means making someone feel slightly unwell

explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-feeling' usually means hostility; here it is literally feeling ill.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a person mildly unwell or reluctant is to cause them slight sickness.

clue.text: The way everybody can get a seat

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A promise that everyone will find a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British theatre the stalls are the seats on the ground floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A ground-floor theatre position or a church pew is a place to sit.

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words winter, naturally

explanation.surface: Someone stays shut indoors in winter, as is only natural.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters lying across 'winter, naturally'.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine someone, as in wartime, is to shut them up.

clue.text: These elderly ladies act, taking chances

parts.note: to do is to act
wagers are bets, the chances one takes

explanation.surface: Old women behave like gamblers, risking their luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Widows holding a title or property from their late husbands are typically older women.

clue.text: Fat sage getting upset about heartless rogue

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the rest
the word sage is upset, its letters thrown into a new order
a rogue with no heart keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A wise old man is getting angry about some heartless villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting upset' turns SAGE into GASE; 'about' puts it around RE, the first and last letters of 'rogue' left by 'heartless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal fat used in cooking or lubrication is called by this name.

clue.text: The frame of the exceptionally sleek heavyweight

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests something out of the ordinary, so the word sleek is rearranged

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: A boxer's physique: the build of a remarkably sleek heavyweight fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptionally' rearranges SLEEK into SKELE.
explanation.definitionFit: The bony structure supporting a body, or any supporting structure, is its framework.
